subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human provenance contract and sensitive-target enforcement surface should OpenClaw support for exec, outbound messaging, gateway mutations, and node/system.run actions?
rationale: This would create a new security boundary plus config/API behavior, and source inspection cannot safely choose the product boundary, fallback behavior, compatibility mode, or plugin visibility rules.

options.title: Core gateway policy
options.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and denial or stricter approval fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

options.title: Plugin context first
options.body: First land safe hook context such as action classification and input provenance, then let a trusted security plugin implement policy once the SDK contract is accepted.

options.title: Fold into taint umbrella
options.body: Defer this into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution guardrail design so maintainers choose one unified model.

recommendation.title: Core gateway policy
recommendation.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and denial or stricter approval fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is recent work around before_tool_call hook context and exec approval policy seams.
